briefing.headline: Kestrel turn the tide after the break; Harbour’s high press and central dominance ebb, game ends level

first_half.text: Harbour dominated the centre and won the ball high, converting that control into chances and two first-half goals.
Kestrel had limited territorial control, low high regains and fewer final-third entries, struggling to threaten.
The field tilt heavily favoured Harbour, reflecting sustained attacking pressure across the middle.

changes.text: Kestrel shifted to regain central presence and increased centre-channel entries after the break.
Harbour’s intensity and high wins dropped: their high regains and turnover height fell meaningfully in the second half.
Possession and final-third entries swung to Kestrel, who produced more attacking activity and xG after the break.

predictions.text: Harbour would force Kestrel wide and Kestrel’s centre entries would fall by at least 30% — instead Kestrel’s centre entries rose.
Harbour would attack the right more and raise right-channel entries by at least 40% — instead Harbour’s right-channel entries fell.
Harbour’s PPDA would increase by at least 20% as their press waned — the PPDA rose only slightly, well under 20%.
Kestrel would sit compact centrally and cut Harbour’s central entries by at least 30% — Harbour’s centre entries dropped around 40%.
Gregor Molina would drop deeper and Harbour’s high regains would fall by at least 30% — Harbour’s high regains per-window fell by 50%.
Kestrel would lift possession by at least 10% as they pushed forward — their possession rose by 12%.

result.text: Kestrel’s second-half tactical shift produced more possession, final-third entries and xG, enabling them to score twice and level the match.
Harbour’s drop in pressing intensity and high regains removed the high press that had yielded early goals, leaving them scoreless after the break.
The match finished 2-2 as Kestrel’s improved territorial control and attacking conversion in the second half neutralised Harbour’s first-half dominance.
